prompt: Animate the player (idle, run, jump, fall) using an AnimationTree with a blend tree.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to see how movement, jumping, and gravity are currently handled, and confirm which Sprite2D frames or sheet exist for idle, run, jump, and fall.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that drive the Sprite2D frames, setting idle and run to loop.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its tree root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. Build the blend tree with an Animation node for each of the four clips, grouping them logically (for example, a grounded branch for idle/run and an airborne branch for jump/fall).
5. Use a Blend2 or BlendSpace1D node driven by horizontal speed to blend idle and run, and a second blend (or a Transition node) driven by vertical velocity to select between jump and fall.
6. Combine the grounded and airborne branches with a Transition or Blend2 node controlled by an on-floor parameter, then connect the result to the Output node.
7. Update player.gd to activate the AnimationTree, and each physics frame set the blend parameters from the player's velocity and floor state, also flipping the Sprite2D based on facing direction.
8. Run level_01.tscn to test all four states, including walking off ledges and jumping from a standstill, then tune blend values and transition timing for smooth results.

1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to see how movement, jumping, and gravity currently work, and what state values (velocity, is_on_floor) are available to drive animation.
2. Prepare the sprite art: set up the Sprite2D with a sprite sheet (hframes/vframes or frame-based) containing idle, run, jump, and fall frames, and confirm the frame ranges for each.
3. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the Sprite2D frame property, with looping set for idle and run and the correct lengths and speeds.
4. Add an AnimationTree node, assign the AnimationPlayer to it, and set its tree root to an AnimationNodeBlendTree.
5. Build the blend tree: add the four animation nodes, use a BlendSpace1D for the grounded idle-to-run blend driven by horizontal speed, and a Transition (or second BlendSpace1D) node to choose between grounded, jump, and fall, wiring everything to the Output node.
6. Expose the blend parameters (run blend position and the air-state selection) on the AnimationTree, and activate the tree.
7. Update player.gd to set those parameters each physics frame from velocity.x, velocity.y, and is_on_floor(), and flip the Sprite2D horizontally based on facing direction.
8. Run level_01.tscn to test the transitions (standing, running, jumping, falling, landing, turning around), then tune blend thresholds and animation speeds, and check that the collision shape and enemy interactions are unaffected.

1. Confirm the Player sprite art: check that idle, run, jump and fall frames exist (as a sprite sheet or separate frames) and note frame counts and frame rates. Decide whether the Sprite2D needs to become an AnimatedSprite2D or stay a Sprite2D driven by an AnimationPlayer.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the sprite frame property, with looping on for idle and run and off for jump and fall.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. Build the blend tree: an Animation node for each clip, a BlendSpace1D or Blend2 node that mixes idle and run by horizontal speed, and a second blend node (or a Transition node) that selects between grounded, jump and fall.
5. Add an Output node, wire the graph into it, and set the AnimationTree to active in the inspector.
6. Update player.gd to compute the blend parameters each physics frame: normalized horizontal speed for the run blend, plus is_on_floor and vertical velocity to select jump or fall, and write them to the AnimationTree parameters.
7. Handle sprite flipping by setting the sprite's flip_h from the facing direction in player.gd, and make sure the collision shape stays aligned.
8. Test in level_01.tscn by running through all four states (standing, running, jumping, falling), tune blend and transition times so there are no pops, and check that the enemy scenes are unaffected.

1. Add an AnimationPlayer under Player and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that drive the Sprite2D frames or region, with looping set on idle and run. Confirm the sprite sheet has frames for each state, and decide how left/right facing will be handled.
2. Add an AnimationTree node as a child of Player, point its Anim Player property at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree. Leave it inactive until the tree is fully built.
3. Build the grounded locomotion part of the blend tree with a BlendSpace1D that blends idle and run along a horizontal speed parameter. Set the blend points so zero speed is idle and full speed is run.
4. Build the airborne part with a second BlendSpace1D (or an Animation node pair) that blends jump and fall along the vertical velocity parameter, with the switch point at zero so rising shows jump and falling shows fall.
5. Combine the grounded and airborne branches using a Transition node (or Blend2 node) driven by an on-floor parameter, then connect its output to the tree's Output node. Set a short crossfade time so changes between ground and air look smooth.
6. Update player.gd to enable the tree and set its parameters every physics frame from the existing movement state: horizontal speed, vertical velocity, and is-on-floor. Flip the Sprite2D based on movement direction.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn and watch the AnimationTree's live parameter values and the active animation. Check every transition: standing still, running, jumping, walking off a ledge, landing, and changing direction mid-air.
8. Tune the blend thresholds, crossfade times, and animation speeds, then verify the two enemy scenes and the level are unaffected. Save the Player scene and level.

1. Prepare the animation source: add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and make the four clips (idle, run, jump, fall) by keying the Sprite2D frame or region, with loop on for idle and run and off for jump and fall.
2. Add an AnimationTree node as a child of Player, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
3. Build the blend tree: put the four animations in an AnimationNodeStateMachine inside the tree, or use Blend2 nodes to mix ground and air, and wire the result into the Output node.
4. Define transitions or blend rules: idle to run by horizontal speed, any ground state to jump when leaving the floor with upward velocity, jump to fall when vertical velocity turns downward, and air to ground on landing.
5. Expose the blend parameters (blend amount, state machine playback) and decide which values player.gd must drive each physics frame.
6. Update player.gd to read velocity and is_on_floor, set the AnimationTree parameters accordingly, and flip the Sprite2D by facing direction; activate the tree.
7. Check that the AnimationTree is active, the CollisionShape2D is unaffected by the clips, and the other scenes (enemies, level_01.tscn) do not depend on the old animation setup.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: run, jump, fall off ledges, and land, then tune transition times and blend values until the motion looks smooth.

1. Confirm the Player sprite setup: decide whether the Sprite2D uses a sprite sheet (hframes/vframes) or separate textures, and gather the frames needed for idle, run, jump, and fall.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer as a child of Player and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the Sprite2D frame (or texture), setting loop on for idle and run and off for jump and fall.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to Player, assign the AnimationPlayer as its animation player, and set its tree root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. In the blend tree, build the grounded and airborne branches: use a Blend2 or Transition node for ground vs. air, with a BlendSpace1D (idle to run, driven by horizontal speed) for the ground branch and a BlendSpace1D (jump to fall, driven by vertical velocity) for the air branch.
5. Wire the branches through the Transition (or Blend2) node into the Output node, exposing parameters such as ground/air state, run blend position, and air blend position.
6. Update player.gd to activate the tree and, every physics frame, set those parameters from velocity and is_on_floor(), and flip the Sprite2D horizontally based on movement direction.
7. Tune thresholds and transition/blend times (run start speed, jump-to-fall apex, landing) so animations do not flicker at low speed or at the jump apex.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn, checking idle, run, jump, fall, landing, and direction flipping, and verify the CollisionShape2D and other scenes are unaffected.

1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, jumping, and floor detection are currently handled, and confirm which sprite sheet frames exist for idle, run, jump, and fall.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that drive the Sprite2D frames, with idle and run looping and jump and fall set appropriately.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. Build the blend tree: an Animation node each for idle, run, jump, and fall, combined with a Blend2 or Transition node so grounded animations (idle/run) blend by horizontal speed and airborne animations (jump/fall) blend by vertical velocity, feeding the Output node.
5. Expose the blend amounts and the grounded/airborne switch as AnimationTree parameters, and activate the tree.
6. Update player.gd to set those parameters each physics frame from velocity and is_on_floor(), and flip the Sprite2D horizontally based on facing direction.
7. Run level_01.tscn and verify each transition (idle to run, jump, fall, landing) looks smooth with no stuck states, then tune blend times and thresholds.
8. Confirm the two enemy scenes and the level are unaffected, and keep the setup reusable so the same tree structure can be applied to other characters later.

1. Prepare the animation assets: confirm or create sprite frames for idle, run, jump, and fall, and set up the Sprite2D with the right hframes/vframes or swap to an AnimatedSprite2D-compatible setup if needed.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene and create four animations (idle, run, jump, fall) that key the sprite frame or texture, with idle and run set to loop.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, assign the AnimationPlayer as its anim player, and set the tree root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. Build the blend tree: add the four animation nodes and combine them with a state-based structure, for example a BlendSpace1D or Transition node, so ground movement blends idle to run by speed and air state selects jump or fall by vertical velocity.
5. Connect the final node to the Output node and enable the AnimationTree's active flag so it drives the AnimationPlayer.
6. Update player.gd to compute the parameters each physics frame: horizontal speed for the run blend, an is-on-floor flag, and vertical velocity sign for jump versus fall, then write them to the AnimationTree parameters.
7. Handle sprite facing by flipping the Sprite2D based on movement direction, and make sure the flip does not fight the animation tracks.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn to verify smooth transitions between all four states, including landing and walking off ledges, and tune blend times and thresholds.

1. Define the animation set: decide on the four states (idle, run, jump, fall), confirm the Sprite2D's sprite sheet has frames for each, and decide whether the run animation needs left/right handled by flipping the sprite instead of separate animations.
2. Add an AnimationPlayer as a child of Player and create idle, run, jump, and fall animations that key the Sprite2D's frame/region (set idle and run to loop, jump and fall to play once or hold the last frame).
3. Add an AnimationTree node to Player, assign the AnimationPlayer as its animation player, create a new AnimationNodeBlendTree as its tree root, and leave it inactive until the graph is built.
4. Build the blend tree graph: add Animation nodes for idle and run, a Blend2 or BlendSpace1D node driven by horizontal speed to mix them for grounded movement, and Animation nodes for jump and fall.
5. Combine grounded and airborne outputs using a Transition node (or additional Blend2) controlled by an "is on floor" parameter and a jump-versus-fall selector based on vertical velocity, then wire the result to the Output node.
6. Update player.gd to get the AnimationTree and set its parameters every physics frame from existing state: horizontal speed magnitude, is_on_floor(), and the sign of velocity.y, plus flipping the Sprite2D from the facing direction.
7. Activate the AnimationTree, verify the parameter paths match the node names in the blend tree, and make sure the AnimationPlayer is not also playing animations on its own (no autoplay conflict).
8. Playtest level_01.tscn to check transitions: standing still, starting and stopping a run, jumping, walking off a ledge into a fall, and landing, then tune blend times and speed thresholds.

1. Review player.gd and the Player scene to learn how movement, jumping, and floor detection are currently handled, and confirm what sprite sheets or frames exist for idle, run, jump, and fall.
2. Set up the Sprite2D frames (or switch to AnimatedSprite2D / sprite-sheet regions) and add an AnimationPlayer to the Player scene, authoring four animations: idle, run, jump, and fall, with looping set appropriately.
3. Add an AnimationTree node to the Player scene, point it at the AnimationPlayer, and set its root to a new AnimationNodeBlendTree.
4. Build the blend tree: use an AnimationNodeStateMachine as the main node, with states for idle, run, jump, and fall, wired through to the Output node.
5. Make the ground states a BlendSpace1D (idle to run, driven by horizontal speed) and the air states a BlendSpace1D (jump to fall, driven by vertical velocity), then define the transitions between ground and air.
6. Configure transition conditions or advance expressions based on is_on_floor and velocity so each switch happens at the right time, and tune blend and crossfade times.
7. Update player.gd to activate the AnimationTree, feed it the speed, vertical velocity, and grounded values each physics frame, and flip the sprite to face the movement direction.
8. Run level_01.tscn to test all four animations and their transitions, including walking off ledges and landing, then tune timings and thresholds as needed.
